title: Digit workshop: Total receipt
summary: For each reading, produce the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value; the digit sum of 0 is 0. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
Loose digit wheels from an old numbering machine need a handwritten inspection ledger. Sol is closing the print-room account before the afternoon mail. A single total must replace the pile of working slips.

For each reading, produce the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value; the digit sum of 0 is 0.

Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement digitWorkshopTotalReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Helper functions. For each reading, produce the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value; the digit sum of 0 is 0. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with helper functions. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each reading, produce the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value; the digit sum of 0 is 0. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,3,7,0,3]. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 20.
The derived sequence is [4,4,2,4]. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 14.
The derived sequence is []. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 0.

overview: Variation: Helper functions. Build the sequence once, then report exactly what the inspection card requests.
